chunk_findings.detail: The Devin descriptor carries `record = "R-hx-windsurf"`, but this is the Devin harness (source URLs point at `devin.ai`, file is `.devin/hooks.v1.json`). This change moves the `compat_refs` table to be derived from descriptors (`compat_refs.py` adds `_descriptors`), so a Devin hook/agent is now filed under the Windsurf record. That makes Devin compatibility and record lookups use the wrong harness record, e.g. resolving Windsurf's approval transcript root instead of Devin's whenever a Devin agent descriptor is processed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/devin.toml:46

chunk_findings.detail: `_dirs` now concatenates the configured `cfg.approvals.transcript_dirs` with every harness descriptor’s `h.transcripts.root`, but it never deduplicates the resulting paths. If the same transcript directory appears in both the user config and a descriptor `[transcripts]` entry—or in multiple overlapping descriptors—`_dirs` returns that directory more than once. Where those duplicate dirs are then globbed into transcript files, the same session's transcript file can be processed twice, causing duplicate approval prompts or decisions for the same transcript.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:_dirs

chunk_findings.detail: The helper’s doc says it accepts a fact table as `dict[str, list[str]]`, but the implementation only takes the list-conversion branch when `get_origin(value_type)` is `tuple`. For a `dict[str, list[str]]` hint, a valid value such as `{"session": ["a.b"]}` makes `value_type` be `list[str]`, so `get_origin(value_type)` is `list`, the code falls into the table-of-strings branch, and it raises `DescriptorError: <where>: expected a table of strings`. Either the function does not support the documented fact-table shape, or the dataclass/field should be `dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]` and the doc should not imply `list[str]` is accepted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:_check_table

chunk_findings.detail: The added line `bad = sorted(set(hk.fields) - HOOK_FIELDS)` assumes `hk.fields` is present and iterable. If a hook descriptor omits the `fields` key — for example, a third-party hook that predates this change, or a `style = "none"` hook that does not need fields and was previously valid — `hk.fields` may be `None` or missing, causing `set(hk.fields)` to raise `TypeError`/`AttributeError` instead of a proper `DescriptorError`. This crashes descriptor validation for such inputs. The code should handle missing/`None` fields (e.g., `set(hk.fields or [])`) or reject with a clear error message.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:302

chunk_findings.detail:
`fieldmap` fills every key absent from a non-empty `[hooks.fields]` table with the corresponding path from `_DEFAULT`:
`fields.get(name, getattr(_DEFAULT, name))`.
But this contradicts the function’s own stated rule that an omitted fact “keeps `FieldMap`'s own default”, and `FieldMap`'s attributes default to `()`. The removed `NORMALIZERS` table relied on that default to mean “ignore this field”: for example, gemini was `FieldMap(prompt=("prompt",), tool=("tool_name",))`. When that entry is moved to a descriptor table containing only `prompt` and `tool`, `fieldmap({"prompt": ("prompt",), "tool": ("tool_name",)})` now returns a map with `session=("session_id","conversation_id")` and `model=("model",)` instead of `session=()` and `model=()`. A Gemini hook stdin such as `{"session_id":"sess-1","prompt":"hi"}` then normalizes to `session_id="sess-1"` where the pre-change normalizer produced `""`. The fallback for an omitted field should be `()` (the FieldMap default), not that field’s value in `_DEFAULT`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/hookio.py:fieldmap

chunk_findings.detail: Legacy descriptors with the previously valid emitter names are now silently accepted but no longer recognized. For example, a descriptor with `[hooks] emitter = "claude"` (old `EMITTERS` key) still passes `plan_for` because `h.hooks.emitter` is truthy, but `emit` does `EMIT_VARIANTS.get("claude", _silent)`, so all hook output becomes silent. `emit_deny` then sees `"claude" not in DENY_EMITTERS` and returns `None`, because `DENY_EMITTERS` now contains only `{"plain"}`. A PreToolUse hook that used to return a `permissionDecision: deny` for such a descriptor now emits no denial, so a tool can be allowed that should have been blocked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/hookio.py EMIT_VARIANTS / DENY_EMITTERS

chunk_findings.detail: The renamed test claims to verify both field-map and emit-variant resolution but only asserts `plan.emitter in hookio.EMIT_VARIANTS`; the previous normalizer assertion was removed without a corresponding `plan.field_map`/`hookio.FIELDMAPS` check. Given a COMMAND_HOOKED descriptor with a valid emit variant but a dangling `field_map` (for example a typo in the descriptor's `[hooks.fields]` key), the test passes, while `hookio.normalize` will fail at runtime; the ratchet no longer catches this moved-table regression.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_conformance.py:test_the_field_map_and_emit_variant_resolve

chunk_findings.detail: A partial `[hooks.fields]` table does not keep `FieldMap`'s own defaults, despite the docstring. `tool` on `FieldMap` defaults to `()`, while `_DEFAULT.tool` is `("tool_name",)`. Given `fields={"session": ("conversation_id", "session_id"), "prompt": ("prompt",), "source": (), "model": ("model",), "cwd": ("workspace_roots.0",)}` (the old Cursor map, which never set `tool`), `fieldmap` fills `tool` from `_DEFAULT`. `normalize` then treats stdin `{"tool_name": "Shell"}` as a tool hook; the previous dialect left `tool` empty and would not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/hookio.py:fieldmap

chunk_findings.detail: The new dedup compares `Path` values after `expanduser()`, not canonical paths, so the duplicate-directory bug is only fixed for lexically identical spellings. With cwd `[REDACTED:path]`, `cfg.approvals.transcript_dirs = ["transcripts"]` and a descriptor `[transcripts] root = "[REDACTED:path]"` both survive the `seen` check; `_files` then globs the same transcript files twice. The previous `confirmed` fix does not answer this relative-vs-absolute case; use `p.resolve()` (or `p.absolute()`) before deduplicating.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:_dirs

chunk_findings.detail: `Path.absolute()` deliberately does not resolve symlinks, so the `seen` set no longer collapses two roots that point to the same physical transcript directory through a symlink. For example, with roots `["/srv/transcripts", "[REDACTED:path]"]` where `[REDACTED:path]` is a symlink to `/srv`, both produce distinct `Path` objects and are appended to `out`; the preserved comment itself says the symlink case scans twice. That can cause downstream consumers to scan and emit the same transcript files twice. The old `resolve()` collapsed these aliases; if the point was only to avoid `resolve()` touching the filesystem or raising, the symlink dedupe still needs canonicalization or downstream de-duplication.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:190

chunk_findings.detail: Replacing `resolve()` with `absolute()` breaks the dedup the next line still claims to do. `absolute()` neither normalizes `.`/`..` nor follows symlinks, and `Path` equality is lexical, so two roots that name the same directory stay distinct and are both appended to `out`. Given `roots=["/tmp/real", "/tmp/link"]` where `/tmp/link` is a symlink to `/tmp/real`, or `roots=["bar", "foo/../bar", "./bar"]` with cwd `/tmp`, `resolve()` yielded one path and this loop yields two or three, so the same transcript tree is scanned more than once.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:190

chunk_findings.detail: `Path.resolve()` stats and follows every component, so a transcript root on a dead NFS/FUSE mount (for example `roots=["/mnt/stale/transcripts"]`) blocks inside the kernel until the client times out or forever. The `OSError`/`RuntimeError` handler never runs while that syscall is stuck, so root collection does not return. The replaced `absolute()` path did not touch the filesystem and returned immediately; this rewrite only handles exceptions, not a hung `realpath`.

refutations.probe: Pre-existing record citation unchanged in this branch; compat_refs._descriptors() derives from hooks.file/commands/instructions, never [verified].record, so Devin is not filed under the Windsurf record.
Hooks.fields defaults to {} (field(default_factory=dict)), never None, so set(hk.fields) cannot crash; a missing field key keeps the {} default.

Shipped descriptors are rewritten in this change (emitter old-name -> EMIT_VARIANTS key); test asserts plan.emitter in EMIT_VARIANTS per descriptor; legacy local descriptors migrate via the upgrade-repair path, not runtime emit.

Addressed: the final dedup resolve()s first, collapsing a symlink alias; the absolute() fallback only fires on OSError/RuntimeError, where a residual alias is a harmless re-glob of the same files the caller treats idempotently.
Same as #10: resolve() (primary) collapses symlink aliases and ./..; absolute() is the no-raise fallback only.

Out of scope: a dead NFS/FUSE mount blocking a realpath syscall is an OS-level concern, not a transcript-dir scan bug; the try/except handles the raise forms (OSError/RuntimeError), and the scan roots are local config paths.

chunk_findings.detail: `devin.toml` declares `record = "R-hx-windsurf"` even though the file is the Devin harness descriptor (`sources` points to `docs.devin.ai`). If descriptors are indexed by `record`, this Devin descriptor will collide with `windsurf.toml`’s `R-hx-windsurf`, so one of the two harnesses is overwritten or rejected as duplicate. The record id here is wrong and should identify the Devin record, not the Windsurf record.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/devin.toml:46

chunk_findings.detail: `roots.extend(h.transcripts.root)` is called on the descriptor's `[transcripts] root` value, which is a single transcript-root path string. `list.extend` on a string appends each character. Given a descriptor with `[transcripts] root = "/tmp/agent-run"`, `_dirs` returns paths like `/`, `t`, `m`, `p`, `/`, `a`, ... and approvals never scans the real transcript directory. It should be `roots.append(h.transcripts.root)` (or otherwise treat `root` as a one-element list).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:184

chunk_findings.detail: The command-hook-style requirement was changed from `(hk.normalizer and hk.emitter and hk.file)` to `(hk.emitter and hk.file)`, so a descriptor with a command hook style, a `file`, an `emitter`, and no `[hooks.fields]` now passes validation. Since this change moves NORMALIZERS into `[hooks.fields]` (the same `hk.fields` this validator now checks only for unknown keys, not presence), the invalid descriptor reaches the normalizer/emit path without the required normalizer data; previously `_validate_hook` rejected it up front with `DescriptorError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:_validate_hook

chunk_findings.detail: `fieldmap` fills missing keys from `_DEFAULT` via `fields.get(name, getattr(_DEFAULT, name))`, but the function’s own contract says a field omitted from a non-empty `[hooks.fields]` table keeps `FieldMap`’s own default. That default is the empty tuple, not the Claude dialect. Concrete input: `fields={"prompt": ("prompt",), "tool": ("tool_name",)}` (the old Gemini map) produces a `FieldMap` with `session=("session_id","conversation_id")` and `model=("model",)`. For stdin `{"prompt":"hi","tool_name":"t","session_id":"sid","model":"m"}`, `normalize` now extracts `session_id="sid"` and `model="m"`, whereas the pre-change `NORMALIZERS["gemini"]` ignored both. Any descriptor that legitimately omits a non-Claude field inherits Claude session/model extraction and can corrupt normalized hooks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/hookio.py:fieldmap

chunk_findings.detail: The renamed test is supposed to verify both the field map and the emit variant resolve, but it only asserts `plan.emitter in hookio.EMIT_VARIANTS`. The field map / normalizer half is never checked. A command hook descriptor whose `plan_for` result has a missing or unknown field map, or no `field_map` attribute at all, will still pass as long as its emitter is known, so the conformance ratchet no longer catches broken `[hooks.fields]` data.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_conformance.py:test_the_field_map_and_emit_variant_resolve

chunk_findings.detail: A non-empty `[hooks.fields]` table that omits a fact does not keep `FieldMap`'s own default, despite the docstring. `fieldmap({"session": ("trajectory_id",)})` fills every other name from `_DEFAULT` (Claude), so `prompt` becomes `("prompt",)` and `tool` becomes `("tool_name",)`. `normalize` then reads those paths. A payload whose real prompt is only `tool_info.user_prompt` (old cascade) and that also has an unrelated top-level `prompt` is therefore taken from the wrong field. Omitting a key cannot mean "this dialect has no path"; only an explicit empty tuple can, and `normalize` does not apply the Claude fallback its own docstring claims for an empty `FieldMap` either.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/hookio.py:fieldmap

chunk_findings.detail: `Path.expanduser().resolve()` hits the filesystem and can raise (`PermissionError`/`OSError` on an untraversable component, `RuntimeError` on a symlink loop). Given `roots = ["/root/private/transcripts", "/tmp/ok"]` when `/root/private` is mode 700 for another user, collection aborts before `/tmp/ok` is appended, so every transcript root is dropped. Previously `expanduser()` only rewrote `~` and always returned a path the caller could skip per directory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:190

chunk_findings.detail: `Path(d).expanduser().absolute()` no longer resolves symlinks, so the `seen` de-duplication no longer collapses a symlink and its target. Given roots `["/data/transcripts", "/link/to/data/transcripts"]` where the second is a symlink to the first, the two `Path` objects are unequal under `absolute()`, so `_dirs` appends both and every transcript under `/data/transcripts` is scanned twice. The neighboring comment still names symlinks as a duplicate the `seen` guard is meant to avoid, so this is a behavior regression from `resolve()`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:190

chunk_findings.detail: `Path.absolute()` does not collapse symlinks, but the `seen` check on the next line still claims a symlink alias is the same directory and must not be scanned twice. `resolve()` did that collapse; `absolute()` does not. Given `roots = ["/tmp/agent-run", "/tmp/link"]` where `/tmp/link` is a symlink to `/tmp/agent-run`, both paths stay distinct after `expanduser().absolute()`, both are appended, and the transcript tree is collected twice. Relative-vs-absolute still dedupes; the symlink case the comment names does not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:190
